content: Yes, you can start tomato seeds in bunches. One common method is to plant several seeds in the same small container, and then thin out the weaker seedlings after they have sprouted and grown a bit. This can help ensure that at least one healthy plant survives to maturity. Alternatively, you can start tomato seeds in a seed tray or cell packs with multiple compartments, planting several seeds in each compartment. As the seedlings grow, you can transplant them into individual pots or into your garden, spacing them out according to the recommended planting distance for tomatoes.
